title: Air India Completes Heathrow Cabin Upgrade, Adds Capacity to Gatwick and Birmingham
excerpt: Retrofitted aircraft on Bengaluru-Heathrow from August 1 complete the Heathrow transition, Premium Economy reaches Bengaluru, and Boeing 777s bring First Class to Gatwick and Birmingham routes.
body:
• From August 1, Bengaluru-London Heathrow flights use retrofitted Boeing 787-8 aircraft, completing Air India's move to new cabin interiors on every Heathrow flight.
  • The Bengaluru switch introduces Premium Economy on that route for the first time.
  • Flights to Birmingham from Amritsar and Delhi, and to Gatwick from Ahmedabad and Amritsar, move to Boeing 777-300ER aircraft, introducing First Class and adding seats.
  • Reader check: if you are booked between Bengaluru and Heathrow, your aircraft type and cabin options have changed — re-check your booking on Air India's site before choosing seats.

Air India has completed the cabin upgrade across its London Heathrow operation. From August 1, Bengaluru-Heathrow flights are operated by retrofitted Boeing 787-8 aircraft with new cabin interiors, which means every Air India flight to and from Heathrow now uses an aircraft with new, retrofitted or upgraded interiors.

The Bengaluru change also introduces Premium Economy on the route. It follows the July 1 switch on Mumbai-Heathrow, where a combination of new Boeing 787-9 aircraft and retrofitted 787-8s replaced Boeing 777-300ERs that already had upgraded interiors.

More Seats to Gatwick and Birmingham

The other half of the deployment adds capacity outside Heathrow. Flights to Birmingham from Amritsar and Delhi, and to London Gatwick from Ahmedabad and Amritsar, are now operated with Boeing 777-300ER aircraft instead of the legacy 787-8s previously deployed. The larger aircraft introduces First Class on those routes. On Air India's 777-300ER configuration, that cabin product includes First Class suites alongside fully flat Business Class beds and Economy seating.

For travellers from Punjab and Gujarat, the two states that feed the Amritsar and Ahmedabad departures, the change is practical: more seats on each flight and a First Class cabin that was not previously offered on those services.

What the New Cabins Include

Air India's new Boeing 787-9, which entered service on Mumbai-Heathrow, has a three-class layout of 30 Business Class suites, 28 Premium Economy seats and 238 Economy seats. The airline's official description of the Heathrow product lists Business suites with direct aisle access and 79-inch fully flat beds, a Premium Economy cabin in a 2-3-2 layout with 38-inch pitch, and Economy seats with 11.6-inch 4K touchscreens. Inflight entertainment runs on the Thales AVANT Up system, with Bluetooth headphone pairing and a library of more than 3,000 hours.

The retrofit programme behind the Bengaluru aircraft is larger than one route. Air India is refitting 26 legacy 787-8 aircraft with new interiors and repainting them in its new livery, alongside deliveries in 2026 of three new line-fit 787-9s and two line-fit A350-1000s.

Why It Matters for UK-India Travellers

The United Kingdom is one of Air India's most important international markets, and the airline operates 57 weekly non-stop flights between India and the UK, connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Ahmedabad and Amritsar with Heathrow, Gatwick and Birmingham. Demand comes from business and leisure travellers and from the Indian diaspora, for whom these are among the most-used long-haul routes in the network.

The completed Heathrow transition removes a lottery that frequent flyers knew well: whether a given flight would have the old cabin or the new one. On Heathrow services, that question now has the same answer every day.

What Comes Next

Retrofits continue through 2026 as more of the 26 legacy 787-8s return to service, and the new 787-9 and A350-1000 deliveries extend the same cabin standard to more long-haul routes. Travellers booking Gatwick and Birmingham services should see the 777-300ER, with its First Class cabin, as the standard aircraft on those routes from this schedule onward.
